page.layout: One column of running text, with small italic marginal notes on the right and a few on the left. Below the text: a footer line with a catchword and a mark. Running head at the top.

main_text.p: rum[?], & non Imperiorum litera & arcana penes Iesuitas essent. Quae enim secta, post hominum memoriam, magis [illegible, ~6 letters] quae magis, cum seculum abiurauerit, seculi pedisequa, ne dicam magistra ac Domina? Ipsa quae (vt Pontificij ipsi querúntur) Formidolosa Regibus esse Thuan. hist. Anno 1565.{i} coepit: Cuius primus fundator Ignatius Loyola praditor fuit{k} aduersus auum Regis Nauarreni: & Filij patrissant heu! satis Orator Gallus ad cur. Parisien. Anno 1611. bene, sequitur enim apud Oratorem; Nec igitur mirum (inquit) si hic pater tot perfidos filios genuerit. Haec ille de spiritu Ignatiano, quem Thuanus Consiliarius Regius, & Curiae Parisiensis nuper Praeses, suis in Parricidas Elegijs eleganter in hunc modum perstrinxit;

p.i: {1}Atque utinam nunquam tibi crus, dux Loyola secta, Icisset Leuâ missa sagitta manu. Quàm bello plus pace noces! & ad otia versus Crudelis animum vertis ad insidias.

main_text.p: Sed fustibus Illi potius quàm versibus profligandi, non-ne? dicant igitur (si possunt) cur Galli primum, deinde Veneti, post Hungari, Bohemi, aliaeque Respublicae Christianae, caeteris Pontificiae religionis Sacerdotibus intrà fines suos acceptis retentisque, hos solos regnis & ditionibus suis exegerunt? Quoties igitur apud me cogito, (Bellarmine) Te doctrinam istam tàm exosam & planè exitiosam Regibus, quam olim in isthac Societate puer imbiberas, alijs postea propinâsse, duplici de causa dolore afficior; tùm quòd Tu Societatem istam vnquàm noueras, tùm quòd Illa Te.
main_text.head: Bellarmini de suis Principibus simulatam gratulationem esse, & gloriationem inanem.
main_text.p: §. IV.In quorum Prin-cipum gratiâ libri suum scripserit.TAm blanditèr se insinuat Cardinalis in Principum benevolentiam, vt Suada ipsa, puto, si vel maximè vellet maiori artificio in Eorum animos influere non posset: “iactat enim Se merito gloriari posse Ecclesiam Rom. Epist. dedic. “ hâc

page.notes: Printed marks: the reference marks in the text (i, k, 1) and their notes are placed as close as I could read them; the placement of the superscript marks in the margin is approximate. Word over "magis" is overprinted and unreadable. "rum," at the start is a word fragment with uncertain punctuation. The catchword "hâc" is printed at the right under the last line; a quotation mark stands before it. The mark "d" at the foot left is read as a signature. A faint mark at the far left bottom ("I.") was not transcribed. Several marginal notes are faint and partly obscured. Greek and printed spelling follow the scan; "Iesuitas" is given as printed with I, since the scan shows the capital form. Verse lines are kept as one stanza.
